text: Rose Matafeo (/ˌmætəˈfeɪoʊ/; born 25 February 1992) is a New Zealand comedian, actress, and TV presenter. She was a writer and performer on the New Zealand late-night comedy sketch show Funny Girls. In 2018, she won the Edinburgh Comedy Award for Best Show at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe for her show Horndog, collecting a £10,000 prize. She was the first person of colour to win the prestigious award for a solo show and the first New Zealander to do so, joining only four other female solo stand-up comedians who had previously won the award. Matafeo was born in Auckland, New Zealand, in 1992 to parents John Matafeo and Diane Vuletich. Her parents are Rastafarians who first met through the Twelve Tribes of Israel denomination; as a child, she attended monthly services at their local headquarters in New Lynn, Auckland. John, a Samoan man and first-generation immigrant to New Zealand, joined the Polynesian Panthers movement as a teenager and worked in an administrative role at the Rastafarian Church. Diane, a Pākehā New Zealander of Scottish and Croatian heritage, works as a teacher and moved to Kampala, Uganda to teach English in the 2010s. Matafeo grew up in Ponsonby, Auckland, and attended Auckland Girls' Grammar School, where she was head girl; she has two older brothers and describes her upbringing as "quite relaxed." At 15, she began stand-up comedy through the New Zealand Comedy Trust's "Class Comedians" programme and won the "Nailed It on the Night" award at the New Zealand International Comedy Festival in 2007. She has been a regular at the festival since and won best newcomer at the 2010 festival. She became a host of the comedy festival show "Fanfiction Comedy" in 2012 and had success with her solo stand-up shows: Life Lessons I've Learnt from the 60s Based on Things I've Seen on Television (2011), Scout's Honour (2012), and The Rose Matafeo Variety Hour (2013). She won the Billy T Award for The Rose Matafeo Variety Hour in 2013, having been previously nominated for Scout's Honour in 2012. Her 2014 festival show was titled Pizza Party. In 2015, she performed a duo show at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe with Guy Montgomery titled Rose Matafeo and Guy Montgomery Are Friends. She was a TV presenter and host of U Live on the TVNZ U channel from 13 March 2011 until 31 August 2013, when the channel ended. After that, she became a writer for Jono and Ben at Ten. She co-created and starred in the New Zealand sketch comedy show Funny Girls for three seasons from 2015 to 2018. Since 2018, she has played the role of Talia in the ABC comedy Squinters. She appeared on Jon Richardson: Ultimate Worrier as an investigator and on 8 Out of 10 Cats Does Countdown (S19, Ep1) for Channel 4 TV in January 2020. She was a contestant on series three of Richard Osman's House of Games and the ninth series of Taskmaster. After ten years touring as a stand-up comedian, Matafeo said in 2018 she wanted to "take a break from hour long comedy" and instead act more, write more, and direct. She directed five episodes of the 2019 New Zealand TV comedy Golden Boy. In 2019, she made her US television debut as a comedian on Conan O'Brien's talk show Conan on TBS. She appeared on James Acaster and Josh Widdicombe's show Hypothetical on Dave. She currently hosts the podcast Boners of the Heart with comedian and writer Alice Snedden on the Little Empire Podcast Network and has been a guest on Deborah Frances-White's The Guilty Feminist podcast and the RHLSTP podcast with Richard Herring. In 2019, she directed five episodes in the first season of Golden Boy and returned to the show in 2020 as a supporting cast member in the second season. In July 2020, she joined Guy Montgomery on the comedy show Tiny Tour of Aotearoa, travelling across New Zealand. On 20 August 2020, her comedy special Horndog was released on HBO Max. She was cast as the lead in the 2020 comedy film Baby Done. In April 2021, Starstruck, a six-part rom-com created by and starring Matafeo, aired on the BBC (UK), HBO (US), TVNZ (New Zealand), and ABC (Australia). Co-written by Matafeo and Alice Snedden, the show featured actor Nikesh Patel as leading man and love interest Tom. Filming for the first series was delayed due to the COVID pandemic, but a second series was commissioned before filming began. A third series was released in September 2023. In 2023, she guest presented the British quiz show Pointless. In 2024, she appeared in Moana 2 as Loto, an engineer who works on boats, and took on the role of Taskmaster in Junior Taskmaster, a Taskmaster spin-off for children aged 9–11, with Mike Wozniak as the assistant. Matafeo previously dated New Zealand comedian Guy Williams. In 2015, she moved to London, where her then-boyfriend James Acaster lived; she shared a flat with comedian Nish Kumar. The two broke up in 2017. One of her interests is mukbang videos; in July 2018, she made a mukbang video using takeaways from Double Happy Takeaways in Auckland, which was featured on The Spinoff. Matafeo is a supporter of the Green Party of Aotearoa New Zealand and was scheduled to host their campaign launch for the 2020 general election, but was later asked to step down due to a miscommunication within the party.
